title: The Python SDK against Cloud and Branch Connector: legacy client settings and session logout on exit

prose.text: How the unified Python client routes ZTW calls to OneAPI or to a legacy helper is in [[cloud-connector.api.authentication]]. This subject holds the legacy helper's settings and what leaving a client session does to staged changes.

prose.label: Leaving a with block.
prose.text: {{exit-deauth-after-mutation}} {{sdk-says-logout-activates}} {{exit-can-activate}} Whether the service also activates on its own, and the ZIA equivalent, are in [[shared.activation.cbc]] and [[zia.sdk-python.activation-and-session]].

checks.do: For the legacy Python client, that ZTW_USERNAME, ZTW_PASSWORD, ZTW_API_KEY and ZTW_CLOUD are set (or passed in the config), not the ZTC_* names the Go SDK and the provider read.
Whether a Python script that wrote ZTW objects ran inside a with block, whose exit logs out and, per the SDK, activates the staged changes.

legacy-env-vars.statement: `LegacyZTWClient` takes `username`, `password`, `api_key` and `cloud` from its config, falling back to `ZTW_USERNAME`, `ZTW_PASSWORD`, `ZTW_API_KEY` and `ZTW_CLOUD`, and a partner ID from `partnerId` or `ZSCALER_PARTNER_ID`.

legacy-host.statement: The legacy ZTW helper sends requests to https://connector.<cloud>.net and authenticates at its /api/v1/auth path.

env-names-differ-from-go.statement: The Python legacy variables are named ZTW_* while the Go SDK's legacy configuration and the ZTC provider read ZTC_*, so one set of environment variables does not serve both SDKs.
env-names-differ-from-go.conditions: Comparison of the variable names each SDK and the provider read at the pin; not run.

exit-deauth-after-mutation.statement: When a OneAPI client's with block exits and the last service it called was ZTW, the request executor ends the session at /ztw/api/v1/auth, but only if a POST, PUT or DELETE was sent during the session.

quotes: For both ZIA and ZTW services, deauthentication is only performed if mutations (POST/PUT/DELETE) have occurred during the session.

sdk-says-logout-activates.statement: The SDK's code comment and its 1.5.9 changelog say ZTW, like ZIA, needs this explicit logout to activate staged configurations, and that the context-manager logout ensures staged configurations are activated on exit.

quotes: # Both ZIA and ZTW require explicit deauthentication to activate staged configurations
(`/zia/api/v1/authenticatedSession` for `ZIA` and `/ztw/api/v1/auth` for `ZTW`), ensuring staged configurations are activated upon context manager exit.

exit-can-activate.statement: So a Python script that writes ZTW objects inside a with block may see its staged changes go live when the block exits, without calling activate, while a read-only script does not log out; the Go SDK has no such step and activates only on an explicit call.
exit-can-activate.conditions: Rests on the SDK's own statement that the logout activates; no Cloud & Branch Connector help page or API description states it (see shared.activation.cbc:session-autoactivation). The logout targets the last service called, so a script that writes ZTW and then calls another service logs out of that service instead.

same-legacy-host-as-go.statement: That is the same connector host the Go SDK's legacy ZTW client uses.
same-legacy-host-as-go.conditions: Comparison of the two SDKs' URL construction; not run.
